candidates.name: C5 frontier-anode-protect
candidates.role: C4 + cathode R 1.2 um (cut 4C CC depth to ~70% SOC so the anode stops at x~0.66 where OCP_a+eta_a > 0) + anode R 1.0 um (eta_a cut ~20 mV). Particle-size balance is the real fast-charge design instrument: the 4C charge ends at 4.2 V, and the cathode kinetics set WHEN - protecting the anode by ending CC in a safe anode window.

candidates.name: C6 frontier-symmetric-probe
candidates.role: same as C5 but cathode R 1.1 um - probes the acceptance side of the frontier (~74% CC expected); C5 and C6 together bracket the tradeoff curve between 4C CC acceptance depth and anode fullness at cutoff

llm_reason: R4 attribution: anode thickening alone is self-limiting - the fixed initial anode lithiation (0.9) plus deeper charge feedback (finer cathode -> charge deepens 78->81% SOC) means x_a at cutoff stays ~0.73-0.77 regardless of N/P, so OCP_a ~0.05 cannot stay positive under realistic eta_a ~0.05 at 4C. The no-plating ceiling is set by WHERE the charge ends, and the cathode particle size is the instrument that sets it: R_pos 1.2 um -> eta_c ~0.24 V -> cutoff at ~70% SOC -> x_a ~0.66 -> anode potential ~+0.06 V. Two probes map the frontier: C5 (1.2 um, conservative) and C6 (1.1 um, more acceptance). Both also improve manufacturability (single-crystal NMC811 at 1.1-1.2 um is commercial practice vs 0.8 um borderline).
